docs(rfc): propose leased sessions and workload-bound OpenBao contracts (#151)

Co-authored-by: Alex Kanitz <alexanderkanitz@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: Pavel Nikonorov <4646953+pavelnikonorov@users.noreply.github.com>

activity.body:
## Scope

Proposes two provider-owned extensions for needs tracked in [ecosystem #99](https://github.com/elixir-cloud-aai/generic-issues/issues/99) and [ecosystem #100](https://github.com/elixir-cloud-aai/generic-issues/issues/100):

- [Leased interactive sessions](https://github.com/ga4gh/ga4gh-sdk/blob/07ec8d2419233fe0450e8fccc75d38e73aa1afc8/docs/rfcs/leased-sessions.md): ownership, readiness, reconnect, bounded renewal, and route and compute cleanup for a live scientific service.
- [Workload-bound secrets](https://github.com/ga4gh/ga4gh-sdk/blob/07ec8d2419233fe0450e8fccc75d38e73aa1afc8/docs/rfcs/workload-secrets.md): requester, execution-intent, and workload binding for an operator broker using OpenBao JWT auth and KV-v2.

The [RFC index](https://github.com/ga4gh/ga4gh-sdk/blob/07ec8d2419233fe0450e8fccc75d38e73aa1afc8/docs/rfcs/README.md) and [example guide](https://github.com/ga4gh/ga4gh-sdk/blob/07ec8d2419233fe0450e8fccc75d38e73aa1afc8/examples/provider-contracts/README.md) connect the proposals to their executable feasibility checks. No standard TES field, SDK/CLI feature, or production TESK integration is added. Both issues remain open for operator and backend work.

## Evidence

- The separate-process session provider, proxy, and HTML report app demonstrated RUNNING before readiness, authenticated delivery, owner denial, reconnect without a second process, renewal, server expiry after client exit, route denial, compute cleanup, and explicit stop.
- A pinned OpenBao 2.7.2 dev container exercised real JWT auth and KV-v2. A separate QC worker read the static fixture; a different workload, changed intent, expired assertion, expired read token, and revoked read token were denied. The script checks its local public fixtures for credential absence. Containers and temporary issuer material are removed after the run.
- Both scripts were rerun on the updated branch. Local documentation links resolve. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/ga4gh/ga4gh-sdk/actions/runs/43055046412) passed all ten jobs, including Coverage and Pre-commit.

## Remaining decisions and limits

- The session example uses a local subprocess controller and test bearer auth. Capability discovery, durable idempotency, lease-generation compare-and-swap, restart reconciliation, real ingress/WebSocket cleanup, and an operator-approved persistent service remain to be implemented and tested.
- The OpenBao example uses a fixed intent digest and test issuer. Production work needs a versioned canonical digest shared across authorization and launch, requester authorization, attested task-to-Pod identity, a protected broker handoff, and inspection of actual TES/gateway persistence and logs.
- Revoking a KV-v2 read token denies future reads; it cannot revoke a value already disclosed. Dynamic credential revocation is a separate requirement.

These are feasibility findings and proposed contracts, not claims that the full deployment path works today.

## Scope

Adds opt-in exact result reuse to `workflow::reuse` under the `workflow-contracts` feature. A versioned receipt combines the existing typed `ResultRecord` with a declared deterministic recipe, original execution identity and artifact manifest. The caller supplies independent trust in the receipt and a fresh authorized artifact reader. Exact recipe matching, complete conformant outputs, current access, size and SHA-256 checks are required before an explicit substitution returns `ReusedResultRef`.

The returned reference names the original provider and run. This module does not submit to provider B or create a synthetic run ID. It adds no global cache, automatic discovery or new TES/WES field. Refs [#147](https://github.com/ga4gh/ga4gh-sdk/issues/147); coordinated under [#148](https://github.com/ga4gh/ga4gh-sdk/issues/148).

## Review integration

- Updated the PR against current `main`. The diff now contains only the reuse module, its tests, example, and documentation; an unrelated dated batch report was removed.
- Required the receipt's durable origin run reference to agree with its typed result. A regression test rejects a re-pinned but internally inconsistent receipt before artifact access.
- Linked the feature from the root README and clarified Docker context and mount prerequisites for the runnable example.

## Evidence

- Eight focused Rust contracts cover changed inputs and parameters, typed and signed-zero identity, trust, current access, malformed receipts, size and integrity failures, and the fresh recheck on explicit reuse. The library test suite and Clippy also passed with `workflow-contracts` enabled.
- The real local demonstration executed one pinned container task on provider A. Provider B accepted and launched zero tasks. The reuse action freshly read, revalidated and transferred 114 artifact bytes; 342 bytes were served across initial verification, substitution and a corruption check. Changed parameter, revoked access, corrupted or deleted artifact, and untrusted source each rejected substitution with a distinct reason.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/ga4gh/ga4gh-sdk/actions/runs/43058760304) passed all ten jobs, including Coverage and Pre-commit.

## Limits

Determinism is an author declaration, and the caller must construct identity from its current prepared task. A receipt hash is not trust by itself; the caller must independently establish provenance and supply authorized, bounded fresh reads. A successful check does not guarantee later artifact availability. The example uses two cooperating loopback TES adapters and one local container; it does not demonstrate a federated identity system, cloud-provider execution or future savings.

Approved for the RFC and feasibility-prototype scope on `07ec8d2`. The changes, checks, and remaining deployment gates are detailed in the [maintainer review note](https://github.com/ga4gh/ga4gh-sdk/pull/151#issuecomment-6800900836).

Approved for the opt-in exact-result-reuse scope on `7517fee`. The focused changes, real-container evidence and remaining trust boundaries are detailed in the [maintainer review note](https://github.com/ga4gh/ga4gh-sdk/pull/156#issuecomment-6801400687).

activity.body:
Reviewed `07ec8d2` against current `main` (`b5f90ec`) for the RFC and feasibility-prototype scope.

I brought the branch up to date and made these focused corrections:

- The session proxy now accepts only the documented paths and methods, with negative checks for unknown operations and wrong methods. Both prototypes fail explicitly under `python -O`, where their assertion-based checks would otherwise be skipped.
- The RFCs and example guide now distinguish demonstrated behavior from missing provider work. In particular, a real broker needs a versioned, shared execution-intent digest rule; the fixed fixture digest does not prove authorization-to-launch binding.
- Added an RFC index and a root README link so readers can find the proposals and see that they are not shipped SDK features. I also shortened the PR description to the evidence and limits relevant to #99/#100.

Both feasibility scripts passed locally, including the real OpenBao JWT/KV-v2 run. `make check` passed (with existing Clippy warnings), local Markdown links resolve, and [all ten CI jobs](https://github.com/ga4gh/ga4gh-sdk/actions/runs/43055046412) passed on this exact head.

I found no remaining blocker for merging these *proposed contracts and prototypes*. Operator agreement, TESK/Kubernetes integration, durable lease recovery, production identity and handoff, and persisted-record inspection remain open gates in [#99](https://github.com/elixir-cloud-aai/generic-issues/issues/99) and [#100](https://github.com/elixir-cloud-aai/generic-issues/issues/100); this PR does not close them.

Reviewed `7517fee` against current `main` (`40fd9d5`) for the opt-in exact-result-reuse scope in #147.

The review pass kept the published diff to the reuse module, its tests, runnable example and documentation. I removed an unrelated dated batch report, linked the new guide from the root README, and corrected the Docker context instructions after verifying that `default` has no daemon on this setup. The receipt now checks that its durable origin run reference matches the typed result's run reference; a re-pinned inconsistent receipt is rejected before any artifact read. The guide also identifies `prepared_for_service` as caller-supplied context, not evidence of a B-side run.

Verification on the integrated tree: the focused reuse tests, all library tests with `workflow-contracts`, feature-enabled Clippy, and `make check` passed. The real pinned-container example passed with explicit `desktop-linux` context: A executed one task, B accepted/launched none, the reuse action revalidated and transferred 114 bytes, and the five changed-parameter/access/integrity/trust cases rejected as expected. Local Markdown links and Python syntax were checked. [All ten exact-head CI jobs](https://github.com/ga4gh/ga4gh-sdk/actions/runs/43058760304) passed.

The outcome remains conditional on a caller-owned independent receipt trust source, a complete identity built from the current prepared task, and fresh authorized bounded artifact reads. The local example is not a federated identity or cloud execution proof. I found no remaining blocker within this PR's stated experimental scope.

activity.title: feat(auth): get tokens from a caller-supplied provider
activity.body:
## Problem

A client configuration holds a static bearer token. Applications that keep a client for longer than a token lives (long-running workflows, task polling for hours, notebooks) have to rebuild the configuration and the client before each call to get a fresh token. That loses connection reuse and makes it easy to send an expired token. Apps that use OAuth 2.0 token exchange also need a different token per audience (one per service), which a single static token can't express.

## Proposed solution

- [ ] A caller-supplied token provider on the configuration, as an alternative to a static token: Rust a trait (e.g. `fn token(&self, audience: &str) -> Result<String, …>`, sync, with an async variant if the transport needs it), Python a callable (`Configuration.set_token_provider(fn)`).
- [ ] The transport asks the provider for every request (or caches until the token's expiry if the provider says so), passing the service's audience (base URL or configured audience).
- [ ] A 401 after a provider-supplied token leads to one more provider call and retry for replayable requests only; non-replayable submissions are never retried (as today).
- [ ] Errors from the provider surface as their own error, distinct from HTTP 401/403.
- [ ] Tokens never appear in logs, `Debug` output or errors.
- [ ] Docs (Rust, Python, the configuration reference) and tests.

The SDK only calls the provider; how tokens are obtained (device flow, token exchange, refresh) stays with the application or with later SDK features such as #90.

Relates to #203 (one authentication contract across SDK, Python and CLI) and #31: the provider should be one of the credential sources that #203 defines, with the same precedence and conflict rules.

This issue was written by Claude Code Opus 5.5 on behalf of @uniqueg.
